versions.title_at_revision: Verify that the stores separate safely from the air vehicle throughout the air vehicle/store launch or jettison flight envelope.
versions.text: Verify that the stores separate safely from the air vehicle throughout the air vehicle/store launch or jettison flight envelope.

Criterion: Verify that the stores separate safely from the air vehicle throughout the air vehicle/store launch or jettison flight envelope. Standard: Stores can be jettisoned throughout the vehicle/store employment flight envelope without inducing dangerous aerodynamic loads and moments, engine damage, propeller damage, store-aircraft collision, damage to any aircraft surface, or damage or interference to critical control functions. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, demonstration, simulation, inspection and review of documentation. Safe separation is verified by Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) models, wind-tunnel testing, safe separation flight testing, and requirements of MIL-STD-1289 and guidance specified in MIL-HDBK-244 and MIL-HDBK-1763. For USAF only, SEEK EAGLE certification is used. References: MIL-STD-1289 MIL-HDBK-244 MIL-HDBK-1763

Standard: Separation of stores does not result in store-to-store or store-to-air vehicle contact, damage, or exceedance of store or air vehicle design loads during jettison and employment. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Perform analysis to assure positive miss distance is expected and maintained during the store separation phase. Assure analysis methods utilize best practices (wind tunnel testing or CFD) for determination of aerodynamic loads. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Perform separation wind tunnel testing of the store and the air vehicle to characterize store separation behavior for all expected modes of separation (e.g., jettison, release) for all mixed load configurations IAW MIL-HDBK-1763, Test 140 and Test 144. Determine employment envelope that prohibits release conditions where there exists potential to have store-to-store or store-to-air vehicle recontact during store separation.
  (2) Ground test: Characterize bomb rack ejection dynamics and effects from lanyards, arming wires, or other external mechanical forces IAW MIL-HDBK-1763, Test 110. Update separation analyses with data collected from ground test. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Analysis.
(2) Perform post-flight separation analysis validating model results to test data. Analysis identifies configurations and flight envelopes IAW MIL-HDBK-1763, Separation Analysis paragraph. Demonstration.
  (1) Show store-to-store and store-to-air vehicle safe separation compliance through execution in a relevant environment IAW MIL-HDBK-1763, Test 271 and Test 272. The number of separation events is informed by the safe separation analysis to determine regions of the employment envelope that show potential for store-to-store or store-to-air vehicle recontact. Test.
(3) Flight test: Conduct store separation test to measure store trajectory and observe store-to-store and store-to-air vehicle miss distance IAW MIL-STD-1289, Clearances Section. Separation testing is accomplished IAW MIL-HDBK-1763, Test 144, Test 270 and Test 280 with separation test vehicle(s) that match system attributes of store variants being certified for fielding or operational use. System attributes include OML, general mass properties (e.g., weight, CG, moments of inertia), aerodynamic performance, and deployment of control surfaces.
